applies_why: The judge text addresses a chain collision but relies on the sign verse's own failure to state the mechanism, so K-C's chain-footing requirement governs.
quote: the sign itself does not state the mechanism.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: Phrase: never verse by verse; reading 1: the judge may not decide by one verse's silence or non-statement; reading 2: it only forbids tallying verses without chain footing.
why: The judge uses Isaiah 7:14's own silence about the mechanism as a reason instead of weighing the pressed chain against the answering chain by footing.
